author: Adam Rex

book_summary: Told from the point of view of a newly-built school, this story follows Frederick Douglass Elementary as he nervously anticipates his first day filled with children. Despite an embarrassing accidental fire alarm and squirting a bullying child with a water fountain, School comes to feel proud and ready by the end of the day, especially after a scared little girl warms up to him and draws him a glittery picture.

fringe_justifications.janitor: The janitor visits School throughout the summer and reassures him children are coming soon; "the janitor comes to visit him, but the janitor assures him others will be there soon."
fringe_justifications.children: The whole plot centers on whether School will like "being filled with children, even if they get everywhere and make messes."
fringe_justifications.teacher: In the kindergarten classroom scene, several children are so frightened that "the teacher must take special care to calm them."
fringe_justifications.fire alarm: A key embarrassing plot event is when School's fire alarm accidentally goes off during the day.
fringe_justifications.water fountain: In a specific comic scene, School squirts a bullying kid in the face using one of his water fountains, then immediately regrets it.
fringe_justifications.nervous: The opening premise states "everyone's just a little bit nervous, especially the school itself," setting up School's central emotional arc.
fringe_justifications.scared: A specific character, "a little girl with freckles," is scared of school and is a recurring figure School worries about winning over.
fringe_justifications.picture: At the end of the book, the freckled girl makes School "a beautiful picture of him," symbolizing her turnaround.
fringe_justifications.glitter: The girl's picture of School is specifically described as "complete with glitter," a distinct visual detail from the book's climax.
fringe_justifications.hug: Reviewers note the illustrations make readers want to give the personified building "a hug," reflecting the book's warm physical/emotional tone toward School.
fringe_justifications.relieved: By day's end School feels a "sigh of relief" as he realizes "she feels capable of being a school," resolving his opening anxiety.

grounding_note: Confirmed via multiple sources (Goodreads, Amazon, Macmillan, School Library Journal review excerpt, Publishers Weekly, and a detailed plot recap from kidsbookaday.com) that this is the 2016 Adam Rex / Christian Robinson picture book about a newly-built, personified school named Frederick Douglass Elementary experiencing first-day jitters, including the janitor, fire alarm incident, water fountain squirt scene, and the freckled girl's glittery drawing at the end.
